The CI for learned minus threshold admitted rate is [+0.412, +0.491], favoring the fixed rule, so the confound is controlled and claim 2 is not_supported. L3s and L3h intervals reach or exceed zero. E03 compares the real LearnedAllocator with the label-free ThresholdAllocator at identical calls (750) and no information advantage. The paired CI for learned minus threshold admitted is [+0.412, +0.491], favoring the fixed rule. L3a and L3b agree. L3p's later pass for the scaled greedy variant failed to hold in L3s, where the interval reaches zero. So the confound is controlled and claim 2 is not_supported. For claim 3, every post-E01 entry reuses E01's pool, so the kill rule's different-model/task/proxy requirement is unmet. L3k shows embedding-only AUC 0.60 and no gain from adding embeddings, and no entry reaches 0.05 AUC gain or 1.5 neighbor ratio, so claim 3 is open.

E03 replays the real label-free ThresholdAllocator against the learned allocator at identical verifier calls (750 at 25%). The paired CI for learned minus threshold admitted rate is [+0.412, +0.491], which favors the fixed rule. The threshold has no free labels, so the free-label confound is controlled. Later work agrees: L3s has a percentile upper bound of +0.0023, and L3h has U_A of +0.0027. Both span zero or favor the threshold. Claim 3 is not killed because every entry uses the E01 pool, with the same model, task and proxy, so no non-E01 entry exists. It is not supported either, since no entry shows an embedding AUC gain of 0.05 or a neighbor ratio of 1.5. It stays open.
